c_opt: Unilateral enlargement and loss of cross-striations of peripheral nerves (sciatic, brachial) and lack of bursal enlargement

Tumorous nodular enlargement of the Bursa of Fabricius in birds under 14 weeks
qText: In poultry, Marek's Disease is distinguished from Avian Leukosis at necropsy by which of the following pathognomonic features?

c_opt: Bursa of Fabricius, which is enlarged, edematous, hyperemic, and covered with a gelatinous yellowish transudate

qText: The primary target organ and earliest gross lesion in chickens suffering from acute Infectious Bursal Disease (IBD / Gumboro) is:

c_opt: Pinpoint petechial hemorrhages on the tips of the proventricular papillae and necrotic button-like ulcers on cecal tonsils
d_opts: Extensive pseudomembranous enteritis of the duodenal loop only
Diffuse fibrous stricture of the gizzard
Caseous diphtheritic plaques confined to the cloaca
qText: The pathognomonic macroscopic lesion in the alimentary tract of chickens infected with velogenic viscerotropic Newcastle Disease (vvND) is:

c_opt: Swollen pale kidneys with tubules distended with urates, along with cystic oviducts producing watery albumin and wrinkled eggshells ('false layers')
d_opts: Exclusive enlargement of the sciatic nerve
Severe granulomatous osteomyelitis with normal egg laying
Fibrinous pericarditis and perihepatitis with intact kidneys
qText: In layer hens, infection with nephropathogenic strains of Infectious Bronchitis Virus (IBV) causes which combination of pathology?

c_opt: Fowl Adenovirus serotype 4 (FAdV-4)
qText: Hydropericardium Syndrome ('Litchi Heart Disease' / Angara Disease) in broiler chicks is caused by:

c_opt: Vitamin E (frequently precipitated by high dietary unsaturated fatty acids)
qText: 'Crazy Chick Disease' (Nutritional Encephalomalacia) in broiler chicks is caused by deficiency of:

c_opt: Non-calcifying caseous granulomas with abundant acid-fast bacilli predominantly in the liver, spleen, and intestines, with lungs rarely affected
d_opts: Heavily calcified pulmonary nodules like in human TB
Exclusive involvement of the comb and wattles
Massive neutrophilic abscesses in the bursa
qText: Avian Tuberculosis caused by Mycobacterium avium is distinguished from other avian granulomatous diseases by forming:

c_opt: Petechial hemorrhages on the epicardium and proventricular fat, multiple focal necrotic white spots in the liver, and consolidated lungs
d_opts: Severe thickening and corrugation of the colon mucosa
Enlarged Bursa of Fabricius with caseous plug
qText: The distinctive pathological finding in 'Fowl Cholera' (Pasteurella multocida) in turkeys and chickens at necropsy is:

c_opt: Fibrinous pericarditis, fibrinous perihepatitis, and fibrinous air sacculitis
qText: The 'colisepriceptic triad' observed at necropsy in broiler chickens suffering from systemic Escherichia coli infection comprises:

c_opt: Ostertagia ostertagi (Ostertagiasis)
qText: In cattle, 'Morocco leather' appearance (nodular cobblestone appearance of the abomasal mucosa) is pathognomonic for:

c_opt: Oesophagostomum columbianum (Nodular worm)
qText: In sheep, the gross lesion known as 'pimply gut' (multiple caseous or calcified submucosal nodules in the intestines) is caused by:

c_opt: Severe intravascular hemolysis, port-wine colored urine (hemoglobinuria), and a gun-metal dark spleen ('blackberry jam')
d_opts: Extensive caseous lymphadenitis of mesenteric nodes
qText: The pathognomonic post-mortem finding in sheep suffering from acute copper poisoning is:

c_opt: Strongylus vulgaris (4th-stage larvae)
qText: In horses, verminous arteritis and thrombosis of the cranial mesenteric artery resulting in thromboembolic colic is caused by migrating larvae of:

c_opt: Acid-fast intranuclear inclusion bodies in renal proximal tubular epithelial cells
d_opts: Extensive amyloid deposition in the mesangium
qText: In dogs with chronic lead poisoning (plumbism), the pathognomonic histological lesion found in the kidneys is:

c_opt: Bright cherry-red blood that fails to clot normally and congestion of mucous membranes
d_opts: Dark chocolate-brown blood due to methemoglobinemia
Thick tarry black blood with splenomegaly
qText: The characteristic post-mortem finding in cattle suffering from acute cyanide (HCN / prussic acid) poisoning (e.g. from immature sorghum ingestion) is:

c_opt: Dark chocolate-brown color due to extensive conversion of hemoglobin to methemoglobin
d_opts: Pale pink color with fat droplets
qText: In contrast to cyanide, acute nitrate/nitrite poisoning in ruminants produces blood that is pathognomonic for having a:

c_opt: Extensive necrosis and apoptosis of B-lymphocytes in lymphoid follicles with interfollicular gelatinous edema
d_opts: Diffuse squamous metaplasia of bursal plicae
Neoplastic pleomorphic T-lymphocytic infiltration without follicle depletion
qText: The definitive microscopic lesion distinguishing the Bursa of Fabricius in acute Infectious Bursal Disease (IBD) from Marek's disease is:

c_opt: Infectious Bursal Disease (IBD / Gumboro)
qText: In broiler chicks, intramuscular hemorrhages on the pectoral (breast) and thigh muscles are a prominent gross necropsy finding in:

c_opt: Foreign-body granulomas with radial urate crystals surrounded by multinucleated giant cells and macrophages
d_opts: Pure suppurative microabscesses rich in heterophils
Eosinophilic granulomas rich in Charcot-Leyden crystals
Dense coagulative necrosis with no cellular response
qText: The primary histological reaction elicited in tissues by articular gout tophi in poultry consists of:

c_opt: Retroviridae (Alpharetrovirus)
qText: Avian Leukosis / Sarcoma group of viruses belong to which family of animal viruses?

c_opt: Siadenovirus (Marble Spleen Disease Virus)
qText: The characteristic post-mortem finding of 'marble spleen' (diffuse splenomegaly with gray-white marbling) in ring-necked pheasants is caused by:

c_opt: Presence of multiple basic amino acids (arginine and lysine) at the cleavage site of the F0 fusion glycoprotein

qText: The primary molecular determinant of systemic virulence in Newcastle Disease Virus is:

c_opt: Cyanosis and edema of the comb and wattles, subcutaneous petechial hemorrhages on the shanks, and diffuse necrosis in multiple organs
d_opts: Proliferative nodular scabs on comb and eyelids
Enlarged sciatic nerves with loss of striations
qText: In chickens suffering from Avian Influenza caused by Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI) H5N1, the classical gross lesions include:

c_opt: Circular, depressed, saucer-shaped necrotic areas with raised borders (target-like / bulls-eye lesions)
d_opts: Diffuse bronze green discoloration without necrosis
Extensive caseous granulomas with concentric calcification
Multiple pinpoint petechial hemorrhages with fatty change
qText: The distinctive necropsy appearance of the liver in turkeys suffering from 'Blackhead' (Histomoniasis / Enterohepatitis) is:

c_opt: Heterakis gallinarum (the cecal nematode)
qText: The intermediate vector responsible for transmitting the protozoan Histomonas meleagridis inside its eggs to turkeys is:

c_opt: Permanent in copula 'Y-shaped' red nematodes attached to the tracheal mucosa, causing hemorrhagic tracheitis and gasping ('gapes')
d_opts: Severe thickening of the crop mucosa
Massive nodular lesions in the gizzard
qText: The pathognomonic lesion of 'Syngamiasis' (Gapeworm disease) in game birds and young poultry caused by Syngamus trachea is:

c_opt: Transverse white ladder-like or staircase-like streaks and plaques on the mucosal surface
d_opts: Deep necrotic crater ulcers in the ileum
Massive hemorrhagic distension of the cecal pouches
qText: Eimeria acervulina infection in poultry is characterized pathologically by which distinctive mucosal lesions in the duodenum?

c_opt: Misshapen, pedunculated, angular, greenish-brown or cystic ovarian follicles containing caseous material
d_opts: Multiple hydatid cysts in the ovary
Complete absence of the left ovary
Diffuse squamous cell carcinoma of the oviduct
qText: In adult carrier hens, Pullorum Disease (Salmonella enterica serovar Pullorum) produces pathognomonic macroscopic ovarian lesions consisting of:

c_opt: Enlarged, friable liver exhibiting a characteristic greenish-bronze metallic sheen
d_opts: Extensive nutmeg pattern of chronic congestion
Miliary white pinpoint foci without discoloration
qText: The pathognomonic necropsy finding in the liver of adult birds suffering from Fowl Typhoid (Salmonella enterica serovar Gallinarum) is:

c_opt: Clostridium perfringens (Types A and C producing NetB toxin)
qText: Necrotic Enteritis in broiler chickens is caused by which toxigenic bacterium proliferating in the small intestine?

c_opt: Microsporum gallinae (Lophophyton gallinae)
qText: Favus ('White Comb') in domestic fowl is a chronic dermatophytosis characterized by white chalky scaling on the comb and wattles, caused by:

c_opt: Central chromatolysis of neurons in brainstem nuclei (e.g. nucleus motorius) and perivascular lymphocytic cuffing
d_opts: Suppurative microabscesses in the cerebral cortex
Demyelination of the optic nerve only
qText: Avian Encephalomyelitis (AE / Epidemic Tremor) in young chicks is characterized histopathologically by pathognomonic:

c_opt: A persistent, unvascularized, unmineralized plug of avascular cartilage in the proximal metaphysis of the tibiotarsus

Complete failure of the periosteum to form bone
qText: Tibial Dyschondroplasia (TD) in fast-growing broiler chickens is pathologically characterized by:

Traumatic fracture of the sciatic nerve by cage wire
qText: Cage Layer Fatigue in commercial caged laying hens is characterized by acute paralysis and osteoporosis caused by:

c_opt: Mismatch between rapid muscle growth and inadequate pulmonary vascular capacity, leading to hypoxia, pulmonary hypertension, and right-sided congestive heart failure
d_opts: Congenital absence of the pericardial sac
Primary hepatic cirrhosis caused by aflatoxins
Excessive dietary sodium chloride leading to primary renal failure
qText: Ascites Syndrome (Pulmonary Hypertension Syndrome / Water Belly) in fast-growing meat-type broilers is fundamentally initiated by:

c_opt: Supracoracoideus (pectoralis minor) muscle encased within an inelastic fascial sheath
qText: Deep Pectoral Myopathy ('Green Muscle Disease') in heavy broilers and turkeys is an ischemic necrosis of which specific muscle?

c_opt: Visceral gout (pericardial/hepatic/serosal urate deposits) and Articular gout (synovial/periarticular deposits)
qText: In poultry, Gout is classified anatomically into two distinct syndromes:

c_opt: Swollen, pale, yellow-tan liver with multifocal petechiae and ecchymoses, containing basophilic intranuclear inclusion bodies in hepatocytes
d_opts: Extensive bile duct carcinoma with metastases
Severe gallbladder distension with clear fluid
Diffuse granulomatous hepatitis with giant cells
qText: The primary macroscopic lesion of 'Inclusion Body Hepatitis' (IBH) in broiler chickens is:

c_opt: Eruptive, hemorrhagic, and necrotizing mucosal lesions with longitudinal diphtheritic bands in the esophagus and cloaca
d_opts: Pure suppurative pneumonia with pulmonary marbling
Severe osteopetrosis with thickening of long bones
Loss of all flight feathers without visceral changes
qText: In ducks, Duck Viral Enteritis (Duck Plague) is caused by an Anatid alphaherpesvirus that produces pathognomonic:

c_opt: Sudden death with ducklings dying in opisthotonos ('stargazing') position and swollen liver covered with punctate hemorrhages
d_opts: Chronic respiratory rales and air sacculitis
Extensive subcutaneous edema of the neck only
qText: Duck Viral Hepatitis (DVH Type 1) in ducklings under 3 weeks of age is an acute, rapidly fatal picornavirus infection characterized by:

d_opts: Rapid osteoclastic bone resorption with fibrous tissue replacement
Multiple subchondral cysts in the femur
qText: Avian Leukosis virus induces 'Osteopetrosis' ('Marble Bone' / 'Boot-leg Disease') in growing chickens by stimulating:

c_opt: Tracheal epithelium and conjunctival mucosa during the early acute stage (first 3 to 5 days)
qText: The specific anatomical site of choice for collecting diagnostic tissue sections to demonstrate Cowdry Type A intranuclear inclusions in chickens with Infectious Laryngotracheitis is:

c_opt: Avian Astroviruses, Reoviruses, and Parvoviruses
qText: In chickens, Infectious Stunting Syndrome (Runting-Stunting Syndrome / Malabsorption Syndrome) is characterized by pancreatic atrophy and cystic dilation of crypts, commonly associated with:

c_opt: Tiny, red-staining intracytoplasmic elementary bodies within mononuclear phagocytic cells
qText: The diagnostic feature that confirms Avian Chlamydiosis (Ornithosis / Psittacosis caused by Chlamydia psittaci) in air sac and liver smears stained with Macchiavello, Stamp's, or Gimenez stain is:

c_opt: Cranial ventral wall of the reticulum, the diaphragm, and the parietal pericardium
d_opts: Dorsal sac of the rumen and spleen
qText: In cattle, Traumatic Reticulopericarditis (TRP / 'Hardware Disease') is initiated when a swallowed foreign metallic body perforates the:

c_opt: Right ventricular hypertrophy and dilation secondary to pulmonary hypertension caused by primary chronic lung disease
d_opts: Primary congenital stenosis of the aortic valve
Acute myocardial infarction of the interventricular septum
Left ventricular dilation caused by systemic hypertension
qText: The term 'Cor Pulmonale' refers to:

c_opt: Chronic alveolar hypoxia triggering severe pulmonary arteriolar vasoconstriction, medial hypertrophy, pulmonary hypertension, and right heart failure

qText: High Altitude Disease ('Brisket Disease') in cattle grazing at elevations above 2,500 meters is caused by:

c_opt: Aortic 'saddle thrombus' at the iliac trifurcation causing hindlimb paresis and ischemic necrosis
d_opts: Renal vein thrombosis leading to nephrotic syndrome
Dissecting aneurysm of the pulmonary trunk
qText: In cats, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is the most frequent cardiac disease, commonly accompanied by which severe vascular complication?

c_opt: Cranioventral consolidation of the lungs with primary aerogenous entry via the bronchial tree
d_opts: Diffuse caudodorsal rubbery consolidation without airway exudation
Absence of any exudate in bronchioles
Exclusive hematogenous dissemination to pleura only
qText: Bronchopneumonia in domestic animals is pathologically characterized by:

c_opt: Acute fibrinous bronchopneumonia (pleuropneumonia) with coagulative necrosis and oat-shaped degenerate leukocytes
d_opts: Pure granulomatous pneumonia with Langhans giant cells
qText: In feedlot cattle, 'Shipping Fever' (Bovine Pneumonic Pasteurellosis) caused by Mannheimia haemolytica produces which specific type of pneumonia?

c_opt: Fusobacterium necrophorum and Trueperella pyogenes
qText: Aspiration pneumonia in ruminants (e.g. from faulty drenching or cleft palate) is characterized by acute necrotizing bronchopneumonia with a foul putrid odor, caused by secondary anaerobic invasion by:

c_opt: Secretory diarrhea with no microscopic damage to the enterocyte brush border (intact villi)
d_opts: Severe villus blunting and crypt cell necrosis
Granulomatous infiltration of the lamina propria
qText: Bovine Neonatal Enteritis caused by Enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli (ETEC) produces diarrhea through which pathological mechanism?

Smooth muscle layers of the muscularis
qText: Rotaviral and Coronaviral enteritis in calves and piglets produce malabsorptive diarrhea by selectively causing necrosis and sloughing of:

qText: In sheep and cattle, acute Ruminal Lactic Acidosis (Grain Overload / Carbohydrate Engorgement) leads to which chemical and microbiological cascade?

Diffuse squamous papillomas in the omasum
Fibrous stricture of the pyloric sphincter
qText: Bovine Leukosis Virus (BLV) causes malignant lymphoma with a strong anatomical predilection for the abomasum, classically producing:

Suppression of parathyroid hormone secretion by glucagon
qText: In dogs with Acute Pancreatitis, the development of systemic hypocalcemia (tetany) is directly caused by:

c_opt: Megalocytosis of hepatocytes, bridging periportal fibrosis, and biliary ductular hyperplasia

qText: The definitive microscopic lesion of chronic toxic hepatitis caused by Pyrrolizidine alkaloid (Senecio, Crotalaria, Heliotropium) ingestion in cattle and horses is the classic triad of:

c_opt: Phylloerythrin (a porphyrin breakdown product of chlorophyll)
qText: Lantana camara poisoning in grazing cattle produces severe secondary (hepatogenous) photosensitization through hepatic retention of which photodynamic metabolite?

c_opt: Microhepatica with hypoplastic portal veins, absence of visible intrahepatic portal branches, and compensatory arteriolar tortuosity/hyperplasia

qText: Congenital Portosystemic Shunts (PSS) in dogs are characterized histopathologically in the liver by:

c_opt: Glomerulonephritis or Glomerular Amyloidosis compromising the glomerular filtration barrier

qText: In dogs, the pathognomonic lesion of Nephrotic Syndrome (proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia, generalized edema, and hypercholesterolemia) is caused by severe:

c_opt: Birefringent, pale-yellow, fan-shaped or prism-shaped Calcium Oxalate monohydrate crystals in proximal renal tubular lumens
d_opts: Eosinophilic intranuclear inclusion bodies in podocytes
Dense amyloid deposits in Bowman's space
qText: Ethylene glycol (antifreeze) toxicity in dogs and cats produces acute oliguric renal failure with pathognomonic histological presence of:

c_opt: Leptospira interrogans (serovar Hardjo or Pomona) or Escherichia coli bacteremia
qText: The pathognomonic renal lesion of 'White Spotted Kidney' observed in slaughtered calves is caused by focal interstitial nephritis induced by:

c_opt: Corynebacterium renale (along with C. pilosum and C. cystitidis)
qText: Bovine Contagious Pyelonephritis is an ascending suppurative urinary infection in postpartum dairy cows caused by:

c_opt: A proteinaceous colloid matrix mixed with Struvite (Magnesium Ammonium Phosphate) crystals
qText: In male cats, feline lower urinary tract disease (FLUTD / FUS) causing fatal urethral obstruction is most frequently caused by a urethral plug composed of:

c_opt: Anti-Müllerian Hormone (AMH) and testosterone from the male fetal testes
qText: Freemartinism in bovine twins (a sterile heifer co-twin to a bull) results from placental vascular anastomoses in utero that allow which factor to arrest female tract development?

c_opt: Proliferative and scabby epidermal lesions with ballooning degeneration and intracytoplasmic eosinophilic inclusions

qText: In sheep, contagious pustular dermatitis ('Orf' / 'Scabby Mouth') affecting the lips, muzzle, and teats is caused by a Parapoxvirus producing characteristic:

c_opt: Cystic endometrial hyperplasia, prolonged estrus behavior, and symmetrical non-pruritic alopecia
qText: In bitches, Ovarian Follicular Cysts produce persistent hyperestrogenism that leads pathologically to:

c_opt: Inhibin and Testosterone, accompanied by nymphomania or stallion-like aggressiveness and contralateral ovarian atrophy
qText: In mares, Granulosa Cell Tumor (GCT) of the ovary is clinically and pathologically distinguished by producing high circulating levels of:

c_opt: Exhibits prominent astrocytic gliosis and neuronal vacuolation in the brainstem alongside vacuolation in both neuronal cell bodies and the neuropil
d_opts: Produces massive purulent microabscesses in the cerebral cortex
Is accompanied by severe demyelinating meningitis
Is caused by a Lentivirus rather than a prion
qText: The primary histological difference between Scrapie in sheep and Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE) in cattle is that Scrapie:

c_opt: Dynamic or static stenotic compression of the cervical spinal cord by malformed cervical vertebrae (C3-C7)
d_opts: Clostridial neurotoxin binding at the neuromuscular junction
Primary degeneration of cerebellar Purkinje cells
qText: In horses, 'Wobbler Syndrome' (Cervical Vertebral Malformation / CVM) causes progressive bilateral hindlimb ataxia due to:

c_opt: Sarcocystis neurona (or Neospora hughesi)
qText: Equine Protozoal Myeloencephalitis (EPM) is caused by infection of the central nervous system by schizonts and merozoites of:

c_opt: Bilateral symmetrical, pale, chalky, dry streaks in heavily worked skeletal muscles (thigh, shoulder) and the subendocardium of the left ventricle
d_opts: Multiple dark red hematomas in abdominal muscles
Diffuse suppurative myositis with gas crepitation
qText: In calves and lambs, Nutritional Myopathy ('White Muscle Disease') caused by Vitamin E and Selenium deficiency is characterized grossly by:

c_opt: Dark red to brown urine containing Myoglobin (myoglobinuria) without intact erythrocytes in urine sediment
d_opts: Milky urine loaded with struvite crystals
qText: Equine Exertional Rhabdomyolysis ('Azoturia' / 'Monday Morning Disease' / 'Tying-Up') is characterized by acute myonecrosis accompanied by which diagnostic urine abnormality?

c_opt: Prolonged secondary hyperparathyroidism (renal in dogs, nutritional in horses) stimulating excessive osteoclastic bone resorption and replacement by fibrovascular stroma
d_opts: Excessive secretion of calcitonin by C cells
Primary dietary deficiency of calcium in adult horses
qText: Fibrous Osteodystrophy ('Rubber Jaw' / Osteodystrophia fibrosa) in dogs and horses is a metabolic bone disorder caused by:

c_opt: A space-occupying intrathoracic mass (such as pulmonary neoplasm or granuloma) stimulating reflex vagal neurovascular proliferation
d_opts: Primary bacterial osteomyelitis caused by Brucella canis
qText: Hypertrophic Osteopathy (Marie's Disease) in dogs is characterized by bilateral symmetrical, periosteal new bone formation along the diaphysis of distal limb bones, triggered by:

c_opt: Loss of dopaminergic inhibitory input from the hypothalamus due to neurodegeneration, causing adenoma or hyperplasia of the pars intermedia producing POMC peptides
qText: Pituitary Pars Intermedia Dysfunction (PPID / Equine Cushing's Disease) in aged horses is caused by:

c_opt: Hyponatremia and Hyperkalemia with a Na+:K+ ratio dropping below 27:1 (or 20:1)
qText: Canine Hypoadrenocorticism (Addison's Disease) is characterized by bilateral idiopathic atrophy of the adrenal cortex, leading to the diagnostic electrolyte hallmark of:

c_opt: Deposition of Islet Amyloid Polypeptide (IAPP / Amylin) causing progressive loss of beta cells in the islets of Langerhans
d_opts: Complete congenital agenesis of the pancreas
qText: In diabetic cats, the underlying pancreatic pathology responsible for Type 2 diabetes mellitus is characterized by:

c_opt: Central corneal ulceration, marked corneal edema ('steamy cornea'), and deep neovascularization
qText: The primary macroscopic lesion of 'Infectious Bovine Keratoconjunctivitis' (IBK / 'Pinkeye') caused by Moraxella bovis is:

c_opt: Involves purulent inflammation extending beyond the ocular cavities into the fibrous tunics (sclera and cornea)
d_opts: Is exclusively caused by viral agents
Is strictly limited to the anterior and posterior chambers
qText: Panophthalmitis differs pathologically from Endophthalmitis in that Panophthalmitis:

c_opt: Involves massive, rapid accumulation of fluid (up to 150-200 L) within the allantoic sac due to adventitious placentation or maternal vascular pathology

Always results in delivery of a normal viable calf
qText: In cattle, 'Hydrops Allantois' (Hydrallantois) is distinguished from 'Hydrops Amnii' (Hydramnios) because Hydrallantois:

c_opt: Type I hypersensitivity (IgE-mediated mast cell degranulation) along with late-phase Th2-driven cutaneous inflammation
qText: In dogs, Canine Atopic Dermatitis (CAD) is pathologically characterized as which type of hypersensitivity reaction?

c_opt: 59 chromosomes (normal canine 2n = 78)
qText: Canine Transmissible Venereal Tumor (CTVT / Sticker's sarcoma) is cytogenetically unique among animal neoplasms because it possesses a stable somatic chromosome number of:

qText: The specific molecular diagnostic fingerprint confirming CTVT by PCR analysis is the detection of a:

qText: The histological appearance of CTVT cells on cytological smears or biopsies is characterized as:

c_opt: Vincristine sulfate administered intravenously weekly
qText: The chemotherapy agent of choice for treating Canine Transmissible Venereal Tumor, achieving >90% complete remission, is:

c_opt: Histamine acting on H2 receptors of gastric parietal cells, stimulating massive hydrochloric acid secretion
qText: In dogs with mast cell tumors, the systemic paraneoplastic development of gastrointestinal ulceration is directly caused by neoplastic release of:

c_opt: 'Away from the elbow, towards the knee' (proximal humerus, distal radius, distal femur, proximal tibia)

qText: Canine Osteosarcoma classically exhibits a radiographic and anatomical distribution rule known as:

c_opt: Lungs (pulmonary metastasis)
qText: In dogs with canine appendicular osteosarcoma, the most common route and anatomical site of early hematogenous metastasis is the:

c_opt: 0.5% (compared to 8% after 1st estrus and 26% after 2nd estrus)
qText: Canine Mammary Tumors show a marked reduction in incidence if ovariohysterectomy (spaying) is performed before the first estrus, reducing the risk to approximately:

qText: In female dogs, the approximate biological distribution between benign and malignant mammary neoplasms is:

c_opt: Both epithelial/myoepithelial cells and heterologous mesenchymal elements (such as cartilage and bone)

qText: A 'Canine Mixed Mammary Tumor' (Pleomorphic Adenoma / Benign Mixed Tumor) is histologically characterized by the presence of:

c_opt: Spleen (followed by the right atrium of the heart and liver)
qText: Canine Hemangiosarcoma is a malignant neoplasm arising from vascular endothelial cells, with the most common primary anatomical site of origin being the:

c_opt: Langerhans cells (epidermal dendritic cells)
qText: Canine Cutaneous Histiocytoma, a common benign dermal tumor in dogs under 3 years of age ('button tumor'), is derived from which epidermal immune cell?

c_opt: Bovine Papillomavirus Type 1 and Type 2 (BPV-1 and BPV-2)
qText: Equine Sarcoid, the most common skin tumor of horses, donkeys, and mules, is fundamentally induced by infection with:

c_opt: Hyperplastic epidermis with elongated, hyperkeratotic rete pegs ('picket-fence' pattern) and a dermal proliferation of fibroblasts in whorls and interlacing bundles

Pure squamous cell carcinoma with epithelial pearls
Caseous granulomas with Langhans giant cells
qText: Histologically, an Equine Sarcoid is characterized by the diagnostic combination of:

c_opt: 'Keratin pearls' (concentric lamellae of keratinized squames) and intercellular bridges (desmosomes)

Osteoid matrix trabeculae surrounded by osteoblasts
qText: The pathognomonic microscopic feature confirming a diagnosis of well-differentiated Squamous Cell Carcinoma (SCC) is the presence of:

c_opt: Gray horses, located in the perineal region, ventral tail base, and parotid gland area
d_opts: Black horses, on the ventral abdomen
Chestnut horses, on the distal limbs
qText: In horses, melanomas and melanocytomas have an exceptionally high incidence in which specific coat color and anatomical region?

c_opt: Severe paraneoplastic hypercalcemia (PTHrP-induced) and early metastasis to the sublumbar (medial iliac) lymph nodes

qText: Canine Apocrine Gland Adenocarcinoma of the Anal Sac (AGASACA) is a malignant perineal tumor that is characterized clinically by:

c_opt: Pancreatic Beta cells, causing paraneoplastic hypoglycemia through autonomous insulin secretion
qText: In ferrets and dogs, an 'Insulinoma' is a functional neuroendocrine tumor originating from which cell type in the islets of Langerhans?

c_opt: Chromaffin cells, secreting excessive catecholamines (epinephrine and norepinephrine)
qText: A 'Pheochromocytoma' in dogs and cattle is a neoplasm of the adrenal medulla arising from which cell type?

c_opt: Invasion through the basement membrane into surrounding stroma, lymphatic/vascular permeation, and cellular anaplasia
qText: The definitive microscopic distinction between an 'Adenoma' and an 'Adenocarcinoma' is that the adenocarcinoma exhibits:

c_opt: Adjuvanted vaccines (such as Rabies and Feline Leukemia Virus vaccines) containing aluminum adjuvants
qText: Feline Injection-Site Sarcoma (FISS / Vaccine-Associated Sarcoma) is an aggressive mesenchymal malignancy, predominantly a Fibrosarcoma, strongly linked to chronic inflammation induced by:

qText: The Hypoglossal Nerve (Cranial Nerve XII) exits through the hypoglossal canal and provides motor innervation to:

c_opt: Chorda Tympani (a branch of the Facial Nerve, CN VII, carried within the lingual nerve)
qText: The Sensory innervation to the rostral two-thirds of the tongue for taste (gustatory) is mediated by which specialized cranial nerve branch?

c_opt: Obturator Nerve inside the pelvic canal against the shaft of the ilium during dystocia
qText: The 'Calving Paralysis' syndrome in post-parturient dairy cows, characterized by inability to adduct the hindlimbs ('downer cow' with limbs splayed laterally), is caused by compressive trauma to the:

c_opt: 'Dropped Elbow' with inability to extend the elbow, carpus, and digits, and knuckling on the fetlock
d_opts: Severe outward rotation of the hock
qText: In horses and cattle, complete paralysis of the Radial Nerve at the level of the arm produces which pathognomonic postural abnormality?

c_opt: Suprascapular Nerve as it winds around the cranial border (cervical border) of the scapular neck
qText: 'Sweeny' in draft horses is an equine neurogenic condition characterized by prominent atrophy of the supraspinatus and infraspinatus muscles on the lateral scapula, caused by trauma to the:

c_opt: Femoral Nerve (innervating the Quadriceps Femoris muscle)
qText: The 'Patellar Reflex' (knee jerk reflex in dogs) evaluates the integrity of the L4-L6 spinal cord segments and which peripheral spinal nerve?

c_opt: First Intercoccygeal space (between Coccygeal 1 and Coccygeal 2) or the Sacrococcygeal space (S5-Co1)
qText: In cattle, Caudal Epidural Anesthesia is routinely performed by inserting a spinal needle into which intervertebral space?

c_opt: Lumbar 7 (L7) and Sacral 1 (S1) vertebrae
qText: Lumbosacral Epidural Anesthesia in the Dog and Sheep is performed by needle puncture into the epidural space between:

c_opt: Atlanto-Occipital Space (articulation between the occipital condyles and the atlas)
qText: Cerebrospinal Fluid (CSF) is collected in horses and cattle from the Cisterna Magna (cerebellomedullary cistern) at which anatomical landmark?

c_opt: Relaxation and desensitization of the retractor penis muscle, allowing protrusion and examination of the penis
qText: The Pudendal Nerve (Nervus pudendus) innervates the caudal external genitalia, and in the bull, Pudendal Nerve Block is performed to achieve:

c_opt: Zygomaticotemporal nerve (branch of the Ophthalmic division of the Trigeminal nerve, CN V1)
qText: The Cornual Nerve (Nervus cornualis), which is blocked with local anesthetic for surgical dehorning in cattle, is a terminal branch of which nerve?

c_opt: T13 (Last thoracic / costoabdominal), L1 (Iliohypogastric), and L2 (Ilioinguinal) nerves
qText: In cattle, paravertebral nerve block for standing flank laparotomy (such as cesarean section or rumenotomy) requires desensitization of which specific spinal nerves?

c_opt: Sternocephalicus muscle (specifically the sternomandibularis in ox and horse)
qText: The 'Jugular Furrow' (sulcus jugularis) of the horse and ox, accommodating the external jugular vein for routine venipuncture, is bounded ventrally by which muscle?

c_opt: Fibrocartilage (e.g., intervertebral discs and pelvic symphysis)
qText: Which of the following cartilages is completely devoid of a perichondrium, relying solely on surrounding synovial fluid or adjacent tissues for its nutrition?

c_opt: One central transverse tubule (T-tubule) flanked by two terminal cisternae of the sarcoplasmic reticulum
d_opts: One T-tubule and one sarcoplasmic reticulum cisterna (Dyad)
Two T-tubules and one terminal cisterna
qText: In mammalian skeletal muscle fibers, a 'Triad' observed at the junction of the A and I bands is anatomically composed of:

c_opt: Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER) and polyribosomes (absent in the axon and axon hillock)
qText: In neuronal cytology, the basophilic clumps known as 'Nissl bodies' (Nissl substance) correspond ultrastructurally to:

c_opt: Pacinian corpuscles (Lamellar corpuscles)
qText: The specialized sensory mechanoreceptors in deep skin, tendons, and joint capsules characterized by concentric lamellae of Schwann cells surrounding a central unmyelinated axon like an onion bulb are:

c_opt: Space of Disse (Perisinusoidal space)
qText: In liver histology, the microvascular perisinusoidal space where blood plasma filters through fenestrated endothelial cells to bathe hepatocyte microvilli is the:

c_opt: Hassall's corpuscle (Thymic corpuscle)
qText: The diagnostic histological hallmark of the Thymus gland medulla, consisting of concentric whorls of keratinizing and degenerated eosinophilic epithelial reticular cells, is the:

c_opt: Zona arcuata (characteristic of carnivores and equines, whereas ruminants display rounded clusters as classic Zona glomerulosa)
qText: In the domestic Ox and Sheep, the outer adrenal cortex (zona subcapsularis) exhibits cellular cords arranged in arched or loop-like clusters, earning it the histological designation:

c_opt: High Endothelial Venules (HEVs)
qText: The specialized venous vessels in the paracortex of lymph nodes lined by plump cuboidal endothelial cells that facilitate lymphocyte homing from the bloodstream are designated:

c_opt: Ligamentum teres hepatis (Round ligament of the liver)
qText: The adult anatomical remnant of the embryonic Left Umbilical Vein, running in the free margin of the falciform ligament to the visceral surface of the liver, is the:

c_opt: The last thoracic (T7), all lumbar, all sacral, and the first few caudal vertebrae
qText: The 'Synsacrum' of birds is a rigid skeletal complex formed by the extensive fusion of which vertebral regions with the pelvic ilium?

c_opt: Right and Left Clavicles (along with the interclavicle)
qText: The 'Furcula' (popularly known as the 'wishbone') in birds is formed by the ventral midline fusion of the:

c_opt: Pectoralis muscle (Pectoralis major / Pectoralis superficialis)
qText: In domestic poultry, the massive breast muscle responsible for the powerful downstroke of the wing during flight is the:

c_opt: 9 (1 single interclavicular, 2 cervical, 2 cranial thoracic, 2 caudal thoracic, and 2 abdominal)
qText: How many total air sacs (sacci pneumatici) are typically present in the domestic fowl (Gallus domesticus)?

c_opt: Koilin layer (composed of hardened protein secreted by mucosal tubular glands)
qText: The thick muscular grinding stomach (gizzard / ventriculus) of the domestic fowl is lined internally by a tough, wear-resistant, yellowish-green protective cuticle termed:

c_opt: Bursa of Fabricius (Cloacal bursa)
qText: The dorsal diverticulum of the cloacal proctodeum in young birds that serves as the primary site of B lymphocyte differentiation and lymphopoiesis is the:
